battle.name: 布隆迪內戰
battle.brief: 布隆迪內戰始於一九九三年十月，總統梅爾基奧爾·恩達達耶遇刺後，軍方、胡圖族武裝與圖西族民兵在布隆迪境內形成交交局面。一八七〇年已列裝的德國陸軍婆塞德後膛砲（Breech-loading cannon），是其地面砲兵使用的正式型號。

kit.name: 婆塞德後膛砲
kit.history: 婆塞德後膛砲於一八七〇年列裝，置於德國陸軍地面砲兵序列，配置於部隊砲兵單位，負責早期野戰與攻城階段的火力支援。

countries: 1993年10月以後，交戰陣營並非固定。初期是布隆迪中央政府、軍隊與警察系統，對抗在首都活動的胡圖武裝小組；隨著讓-巴蒂斯特·巴加扎、西爾維·基尼吉與帕斯卡爾-菲爾明·恩迪米拉先後掌權，中央一方的政策與族群平衡多次重組，反軍則逐步形成FNL、PALIPEHUTU及CNDD-FDD等聯盟或派系。盧安達在1994年成為武器、人員與情報越境流動的重要來源，但多數時候不是公開交戰國。1996年坦尚尼亞受邀派兵進入布隆迪，1998年南非特遣隊赴布瓊布拉協防；比利時主要在1995年政變危機中提供有限保護，烏干達與薩伊則主要影響邊境通道。三支外軍的任務、規模與持續時間不同，不能混寫成同一場聯合行動；聯合國制裁與武器禁運則透過補給、外交和資金來源間接改變戰局。
countriesEn: The belligerent alignment did not remain fixed after October 1993. Initially, the Burundian central government, army, and police system faced Hutu armed cells operating in the capital. As Jean-Baptiste Bagaza, Sylvie Kinigi, and Pascal-Firmin Ndimira came to power in succession, the policies and ethnic balance of the central side were repeatedly reshaped, while the insurgents gradually formed alliances and factions such as the FNL, PALIPEHUTU, and CNDD-FDD. Rwanda became an important source of weapons, personnel, and intelligence crossing the border in 1994, although it was not consistently a direct belligerent. Tanzania entered Burundi with troops at the government’s invitation in 1996, and a South African detachment deployed to Bujumbura in 1998. Belgium provided limited protection during the 1995 coup crisis, while Uganda and Zaire mainly affected access along the border. The foreign forces had different mandates, strengths, and durations, so they cannot be treated as one joint operation. United Nations sanctions and the arms embargo indirectly altered the war by restricting supplies, diplomacy, and financing.
people: 關鍵人物可由權責鏈條辨認。梅爾基奧爾·恩達達耶是FRODEBU領袖及1993年首位民選胡圖總統；他於10月21日在布瓊布拉總統辦公區域被一批武裝侍從人員殺死，直接主使沒有定論。讓-巴蒂斯特·巴加扎在10月22日重掌國家，10月23日任命胡圖出身的西爾維·基尼吉為首相；這個混合內閣到11月3日即被帕斯卡爾-菲爾明·恩迪米拉推翻。恩迪米拉是軍人而非民選總統，後來出任總理，並與皮埃爾·布約亞共同促成1996年的權力更替。西普里安·恩塔里亞米拉與阿納托爾·卡涅恩基科於1994年2月分別就任總統與總理，4月6日同乘的Beechcraft Super King Air 200墜毀身亡；雖有反軍以飛彈攻擊之說，但發射者與武器型號未定。西爾維斯特爾·恩蒂邦通加尼亞在同年5月當選總統，1995年2月由阿方斯-馬里·卡德熱接任總理；巴加扎於5月27日再奪權失敗。布約亞則在1996年10月27日推翻恩蒂邦通加尼亞，成為後續停火與選舉時期的總統。反軍方面，萊昂納爾·尼揚戈馬與讓-博斯科·恩代延古魯基耶參與CNDD-FDD的建立，阿加松·魯瓦薩成為最具影響力的FDD指揮者；FNL與PALIPEHUTU因地方支派林立而指揮權多次更替。
peopleEn: The principal actors can be followed through a chain of formal responsibility. Melchior Ndadaye, the FRODEBU leader and Burundi’s first democratically elected Hutu president, was killed on 21 October in the presidential office area of Bujumbura by armed members of the protective detail; there is no settled account of who ordered the killing. Jean-Baptiste Bagaza regained power on 22 October and appointed the Hutu politician Sylvie Kinigi as prime minister on 23 October. Their mixed cabinet lasted only until 3 November, when Pascal-Firmin Ndimira overthrew it. Ndimira was a military officer rather than an elected president, later served as prime minister, and worked with Pierre Buyoya through the 1996 changes in government. Cyprien Ntaryamira and Anatole Kanyenkiko became president and prime minister in February 1994, but both died on 6 April when their Beechcraft Super King Air 200 crashed. A rebel missile attack has been proposed, although neither the launcher nor the weapon type has been established. Sylvestre Ntibantunganya was elected president in May 1994, and Alphonse-Marie Kadege became prime minister after a cabinet reshuffle in February 1995. Bagaza’s attempt to seize power again failed on 27 May. Buyoya overthrew Ntibantunganya on 27 October 1996 and remained president through the ceasefire and electoral period. On the rebel side, Leonard Nyangoma and Jean-Bosco Ndayikengurukiye participated in establishing the CNDD-FDD, while Agathon Rwasa became its most influential FDD commander. Command within the FNL and PALIPEHUTU changed repeatedly because both were divided among numerous local factions.
kits: 1993年時，雙方軍火並非同一套制式。政府軍與武裝警察常見FN FAL突擊步槍、AK-47及AKM；固定支援火力包括1933年列裝的Browning M2重機槍、1958年列裝的FN MAG，以及1977年列裝的M240。反軍大量使用AK-47、AKM和FN FAL，另有1961年列裝的PKM通用機槍、1960年列裝的RPG-7、七六公厘步槍彈藥及八十一或八十二公厘迫擊砲；這些武器多來自政府軍繳獲品、境外流動與後續交付，並沒有統一的反軍編配。雙方都可見RPG-7、四一公厘M1式及八十二公厘PM-37式迫擊砲、十四點五公厘KPV重機槍等支援武器。政府航空與總統飛行任務使用過1965年列裝的SA 330 Puma、1967年列裝的SA 341 Gazelle及1971年列裝的C-212 Aviocar；失事的Beechcraft Super King Air 200則於1974年開始服役。坦尚尼亞部隊主要使用FN FAL與RPG-7，南非特遣隊則可見一九八〇年代列裝的R1、R4步槍及FN MAG。陸路機動以Toyota Land Cruiser、1966年推出的Hilux、Land Rover 101與110及卡車為主，反軍把皮卡改裝成裝載機槍的技術車。各單位數量沒有可靠總表，因此只能確認型號與用途，不能臆測兵力配比。
kitsEn: The two sides did not field a single standardized weapon system in 1993. Government forces and armed police commonly used the FN FAL assault rifle, AK-47, and AKM. Fixed support fire included the Browning M2 heavy machine gun, introduced in 1933; the FN MAG, introduced in 1958; and the M240, introduced in 1977. Rebel forces relied heavily on the AK-47, AKM, and FN FAL, together with the PKM general-purpose machine gun introduced in 1961, the RPG-7 introduced in 1960, 7.62 mm rifle ammunition, and 81 mm or 82 mm mortars. These weapons came from captured government stocks, cross-border flows, and later deliveries, and the rebels had no unified distribution system. Support weapons visible on both sides included the RPG-7, 81 mm M1 and 82 mm PM-37 mortars, and the 14.5 mm KPV heavy machine gun. Government aviation and presidential transport duties involved the SA 330 Puma, introduced in 1965; the SA 341 Gazelle, introduced in 1967; and the C-212 Aviocar, introduced in 1971. The Beechcraft Super King Air 200 involved in the crash had entered service in 1974. Tanzanian troops mainly used the FN FAL and RPG-7, while South African personnel carried the R1 and R4 rifles adopted during the 1980s and the FN MAG. Ground mobility centered on Toyota Land Cruisers, the Hilux introduced in 1966, Land Rover 101 and 110 models, and trucks. Rebels converted pickups into machine-gun-equipped technicals. No dependable inventory establishes unit totals, so only the types and roles can be stated without inventing force distributions.
tactics: 戰術演變可分成首都奪權期、農村消耗期、外軍介入期與停火整編期。1993年10月21日至11月初，中央權力中斷使首都數個行政區與軍政設施迅速落入武裝小組手中；忠於政府的部隊依靠營區防衛、路障與逐區清剿奪回控制。11月至12月的街區戰顯示，反軍若長時間停留在宮殿、機場周邊或固定政府建築，便會暴露於政府火力與外軍撤運安排的協調下；多數突擊因此採取短時間衝擊、破壞聯繫後退回山地或邊境据點的作法。1994年至1996年，反軍把作戰重心移往Kayanza、Ngozi、Cibitoke、Isale及南部Mugongomanga、Makamba一帶，利用分散營地、夜間移動與道路伏擊，使政府必須分割兵力。中央軍則以布瓊布拉為樞紐，控制通往Ngozi、Kayanza、Mugongomanga與Rutana的主要走廊，依靠路檢、無線電連繫與定期清剿維持道路，但難以長期占領廣大鄉間。1996年10月至11月，坦尚尼亞部隊由東南邊境向中南部推進，與政府軍共同切開反軍控制區，恢復部分補給線；反軍隨即向西部及邊境山地轉移。1998年6月，CNDD-FDD及其他派系向布瓊布拉北部、西部通道發動協調攻勢，迫使政府把預備隊壓到首都外圍。南非特遣隊的裝甲與步兵小組封住主要進城道路，政府軍才得以迫使攻擊者退回。1999年後，戰鬥重點轉為停火監督、集結區、分批解除武裝與政治代表進入過渡機構，殘餘派系則利用停火裂縫恢復游擊行動。
tacticsEn: The campaign passed through four tactical phases: struggle for the capital, rural war of movement, intervention by foreign forces, and ceasefire integration. Between 21 October and the beginning of November 1993, the breakdown of central authority allowed armed cells to seize districts and government installations around Bujumbura. Units loyal to the government relied on barracks defense, roadblocks, and district-by-district clearance to regain control. Street fighting from November through December showed that rebels exposed by remaining around the presidential palace, airport, or fixed government buildings could be pinned down by government fire and coordinated foreign evacuation arrangements. Most attacks therefore consisted of a brief assault, disruption of communications, and withdrawal to hills or border bases. From 1994 to 1996, the insurgents shifted toward Kayanza, Ngozi, Cibitoke, Isale, Mugongomanga, and Makamba, using dispersed camps, night movement, and ambushes along roads to force the government to divide its forces. The army used Bujumbura as its logistics hub, sought to control the main corridors toward Ngozi, Kayanza, Mugongomanga, and Rutana, and relied on checkpoints, radio links, and periodic clearing operations, but could not hold the countryside permanently. From October to November 1996, Tanzanian troops advanced from the southeastern border into the central and southern interior, cutting rebel-held areas with government forces and restoring several supply routes; the insurgents then shifted west and toward the border highlands. In June 1998, the CNDD-FDD and allied factions launched a coordinated drive toward the northern and western approaches to Bujumbura, compelling the government to concentrate reserves outside the capital. South African armor and infantry teams blocked the principal entry roads, after which government forces forced the attackers back. After 1999, the main tasks became ceasefire monitoring, assembly areas, phased disarmament, and political participation in transitional institutions, while holdout groups exploited gaps in the ceasefires to resume guerrilla activity.
data: 完整時間線可由1993年6月至7月的總統與國會選舉開始；恩達達耶於9月4日就任。10月21日發生總統暗殺，10月22日巴加扎再掌政，10月23日基尼吉組閣，11月3日恩迪米拉再度政變；此後數週的城區戰至12月才讓政府重新控制布瓊布拉。1994年2月5日恩塔里亞米拉當選總統，4月6日座機墜毀使總統、總理、機組與其他同行者全部死亡；5月恩蒂邦通加尼亞當選。1995年2月卡德熱出任總理，5月27日巴加扎趁恩蒂邦通加尼亞與卡德熱出國時發動不成功的政變，比利時部隊協助守住政府。1996年7月的軍政改組由恩迪米拉出任總理，8月28日政府與部分胡圖代表在Arusha達成初步和平安排，10月27日布約亞推翻恩蒂邦通加尼亞；10月至11月坦尚尼亞作戰與政府反攻恢復中南部交通，卻未永久驅散西部及北部反軍。1998年6月反軍攻近布瓊布拉，南非部隊介入後首都保住。1999年8月28日簽署新的Arusha和平與和解協議，部分武裝派系加入，多數派系則在2000年11月組成的過渡權力中才接受安排。2001年至2002年的停火、2002年7月至8月選舉，以及2003年至2005年的殘餘戰鬥，構成最後階段；2005年5月10日，最後拒絕全面執行的武裝派系同意停火與和平安排，戰爭通常以這一天視為結束。補給上，布瓊布拉是主要樞紐，北線沿Bujumbura-Ngozi-Kayanza，西南線通往Mugongomanga與Makamba，東線通往Rutana；主要公路較易維持車輛通行，支線在三月至五月雨季常被泥濘切斷。政府車隊集中於主幹道，反軍更多依賴徒步、接力運輸與技術車，燃料、備用零件、無線電電池及不同口徑彈藥都受數量限制。各方傷亡紀錄分散且口徑不一，本文不列無法交叉核對的精確總數。
dataEn: A full timeline begins with the presidential and parliamentary elections from June to July 1993; Ndadaye took office on 4 September. The presidential assassination occurred on 21 October, Bagaza regained power on 22 October, Kinigi formed a cabinet on 23 October, and Ndimira staged another coup on 3 November. Urban fighting continued for several weeks, and the government did not regain firm control of Bujumbura until December. Ntaryamira was elected president on 5 February 1994. The aircraft crash on 6 April killed the president, prime minister, crew, and the other passengers, and Ntibantunganya was elected in May. Kadege became prime minister after the February 1995 reshuffle. On 27 May, Bagaza attempted another coup while Ntibantunganya and Kadege were abroad, but Belgian troops helped the government remain in power. A further military and political reorganization in July 1996 brought Ndimira back as prime minister. On 28 August, the government and some Hutu representatives reached a preliminary peace arrangement at Arusha. Buyoya overthrew Ntibantunganya on 27 October, and the joint Tanzanian-government campaign from October to November restored roads in the central and southern interior without permanently dislodging the western and northern insurgents. Rebel forces approached Bujumbura in June 1998, but South African intervention preserved the capital. A new Arusha Peace and Reconciliation Agreement followed on 28 August 1999. Several factions accepted its framework, while most were drawn into the transitional arrangement established in November 2000. Ceasefires during 2001 and 2002, the July and August 2002 elections, and residual fighting from 2003 to 2005 formed the final phase. On 10 May 2005, the last armed faction refusing full implementation accepted a ceasefire and peace settlement, the date normally used for the war’s conclusion. Logistically, Bujumbura was the principal hub, with a northern axis toward Ngozi and Kayanza, a southwestern route through Mugongomanga and Makamba, and an eastern road toward Rutana. Main roads could sustain vehicle movement, while side tracks were frequently cut by mud during the March-to-May rains. Government convoys concentrated on trunk routes; rebels relied more on movement on foot, relay transport, and technical vehicles. Fuel, spare parts, radio batteries, and ammunition in several calibres were all limited. Combatant casualty records are fragmented and inconsistently defined, so no unverifiable exact total is used here.
cause: 內戰的成因具有長期制度與短 期政治兩個層次。布隆迪獨立後，人口較多的胡圖人在高階軍政職務、總統府與安全系統中長期受限，圖西族軍官長期掌握核心指揮權；一九八〇年代咖啡價格下跌、財政緊縮及結構調整又削弱政府維持軍隊和行政機構的能力，使軍方與武裝政治團體競相尋找資金與外國支持。一九九一年後開放黨政，一九九三年恩達達耶在FRODEBU領導下當選，並與圖西族的UPRONA組建政治妥協；但新政府未能同步改變軍隊高層權力，因此選舉打開了政治競爭，沒有消除軍方直接干政的結構。恩達達耶遇刺是立即導火線，其後巴加扎、基尼吉與恩迪米拉在十二天內連續改組權力，逮捕與清除被懷疑涉及暗殺或支持新政權的軍警人員，又把原本可由憲政程序處理的衝突轉成武裝對抗。恩蒂邦通加尼亞與卡德熱曾以混合內閣和地方讓步嘗試重建信任，但軍隊指揮、地方行政與武裝派系各自形成安全依附關係。1994年盧安達戰事使槍械、RPG彈藥、步槍及受訓戰鬥人員越境流入，使原本缺乏彈藥的武裝小組能持續作戰；外部部隊與禁運政策後來又改變雙方資源平衡。因此，這場戰爭不是單一暗殺事件造成，而是制度排除、經濟衰退、軍政競爭、暗殺與跨境武器流動共同作用的結果。
causeEn: The causes operated on both long-term institutional and short-term political levels. After independence, the numerically larger Hutu population remained heavily restricted from senior military and government offices, the presidency, and the security apparatus, while Tutsi officers retained control of the core command. Falling coffee prices, fiscal contraction, and structural adjustment during the 1980s weakened the state’s ability to sustain the army and administrative institutions, encouraging military officers and armed political organizations to seek foreign support. Political opening began in 1991, and Ndadaye won the 1993 election under FRODEBU and formed a compromise with the Tutsi-led UPRONA. The new government did not change the senior military command, so elections opened political competition without removing the army’s capacity to intervene directly. Ndadaye’s assassination was the immediate trigger. Bagaza, Kinigi, and Ndimira then changed the government within twelve days, and arrests and removals of military and police personnel suspected of involvement in the killing transformed a dispute that might have been handled constitutionally into armed confrontation. Ntibantunganya and Kadege attempted to rebuild confidence through a mixed cabinet and local concessions, but military commands, local administrations, and armed factions had each developed their own security relationships. The 1994 war in Rwanda sent rifles, RPG ammunition, and trained fighters across the border, allowing poorly supplied cells to continue fighting. Foreign deployments and embargo policies later altered the resource balance. The war therefore resulted not from the assassination alone, but from institutional exclusion, economic decline, military-political rivalry, the killing itself, and the cross-border movement of weapons.
impact: 軍事影響首先表現爲控制區與戰略節奏的改變。政府雖長期保有布瓊布拉、機場及若干主要鋪裝公路，卻難以同時清除北部Kayanza、Ngozi、西南Mugongomanga與Makamba及東部邊境的反軍據點；反軍也不需要控制首都，只要掌握足以切斷城鄉交通的山地與邊境地區，便能增加執政者迫使全面停火的籌碼。CNDD-FDD在1996年後成為最有組織的反軍力量，FNL與PALIPEHUTU的地區支派則使談判代表與前線指揮分離。坦尚尼亞介入恢復中南部走廊，南非部隊則在1998年改變首都立即防務；前者重塑鄉間平衡，後者守住城市，但都沒有單獨終止叛亂。戰爭同時加速軍隊與警察系統的派系化，政變由少數軍人完成，卻常須依賴地方行政、盟軍或外軍維持首都。聯合國制裁、美國與歐洲武器禁運及外部邊境管制，限制了政府與反軍補充外部武器的方式，但也提高跨境作戰成本。到一九九九年底，政府的軍事優勢不足以排除政治協議，而部分反軍派系則利用有利於整合的談判位置完成軍事轉向。各方傷亡數字因紀錄中斷、戰俘交換和不同統計範圍而難以核對，沒有可信的單一精確總量；能確定的變化是首都防務、鄉間控制、外國介入與政治代表結構都已被永久改變。
impactEn: The first military effect was a change in control and the tempo of operations. Although the government retained Bujumbura, the airport, and several main paved roads, it could not clear the rebel positions around Kayanza and Ngozi in the north, Mugongomanga and Makamba in the southwest, and the eastern border simultaneously. The insurgents did not need to hold the capital: control of enough mountain and border country to interrupt urban-rural movement gave them leverage to force negotiations. After 1996 the CNDD-FDD became the best organized rebel force, while regional branches of the FNL and PALIPEHUTU separated negotiating delegates from field commanders. Tanzanian intervention restored corridors in the central and southern interior, and South African troops changed the immediate defense of the capital in 1998. The former reshaped the rural balance and the latter saved the city, but neither ended the insurgency alone. The war also accelerated factionalization within the army and police. Coups could be executed by small groups of officers, but those regimes often depended on local administration, allied forces, or foreign deployments to preserve the capital. United Nations sanctions, United States and European arms embargoes, and external border controls constrained access to foreign weapons while also raising the cost of cross-border operations. By late 1999, the government’s military advantage was insufficient to exclude a political agreement, while some rebel factions used the favorable terms of negotiation to complete their shift toward political participation. Casualty totals cannot be reliably verified because records are incomplete and exchanges, prisoners, and statistical definitions differ, so there is no trustworthy single exact figure. What can be established is that the defense of the capital, the rural balance of control, foreign intervention, and the structure of political representation were permanently altered.
result: 最終結果並非一方在戰場上把另一方完全消滅，而是中央政府保住國家主權，反軍在節奏不利與政治失敗的壓力下逐步接受停火、解除武裝及政黨化。1999年8月28日的Arusha協議建立停火與和解框架，2000年11月的過渡權力吸納政府、議會及反軍代表；2001年至2002年的停火雖被派系違反，卻使多數武裝組織放棄持續控制固定地區，轉而以政治組織參與2002年選舉。布約亞在這次選舉中獲胜，部分CNDD-FDD、FNL與PALIPEHUTU派系進入政府或議會，前軍方人物由此轉成政黨及行政領導。仍有以魯瓦薩派FDD為主的武裝拒絕全面交出武器與遵守既有安排，使布隆迪在2003年至2005年持續進行小規模游擊、襲擊與政府清剿。2005年5月10日，最後的主要武裝派系同意停火並接受和平框架，經過多次延期選舉及過渡政府運作，原CNDD-FDD的政治翼轉為全國政黨，其領袖Pierre Nkurunziza在2005年當選總統。因而戰爭在軍事上以殘餘派系停火及解除武裝告終，在政治上以軍方放棄單獨執政、反軍組織進入憲政體系告終；國家機構與軍隊仍然存在且國家主權得以維持，但長期派系化、軍隊整編和解除武裝進度不完整，仍是戰後安全問題的核心。
resultEn: The final outcome was not the complete destruction of one side on the battlefield. The central government preserved national sovereignty, while the insurgents came under mounting military and political pressure and progressively accepted ceasefires, demobilization, and party conversion. The Arusha Agreement of 28 August 1999 established a framework for ceasefire and reconciliation, and the transitional authority formed in November 2000 absorbed government, parliamentary, and rebel representatives. Ceasefires were violated by factions between 2001 and 2002, but most armed organizations gradually accepted the loss of permanently held territory and entered politics through the 2002 elections. Buyoya won that election, and elements of the CNDD-FDD, FNL, and PALIPEHUTU entered government or parliament, allowing former commanders to become party leaders and administrators. The FDD wing associated with Agathon Rwasa still refused to surrender all weapons or fully implement earlier agreements, sustaining smaller guerrilla campaigns, attacks, and government clearing operations through 2003 to 2005. On 10 May 2005, the last major armed faction accepted a ceasefire and peace framework. Following repeated postponed elections and the operation of the transitional government, the former CNDD-FDD’s political wing became a national party, and its leader Pierre Nkurunziza was elected president in 2005. Militarily, the war ended with the ceasefire and demobilization of the remaining factions; politically, it ended when the military abandoned exclusive control of the state and rebel organizations entered constitutional government. The state institutions and army survived, and national sovereignty was maintained, but incomplete factional reform, military restructuring, and demobilization remained central postwar security problems.
